Subject: Evergreen RFI — key provenance, BYO process, and TLS profile

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this — Evergreen has a short technical RFI focused on encryption and key custody for our evaluation. We need your answers to the following items by COB next Wednesday so we can progress to procurement:

1) BYO keys: describe supported import paths (PKCS#12, PKCS#8, wrapped import tokens), algorithms supported for wrapping, and whether keys ever exist in clear on Redwood-managed hosts.
2) HSM attestation: which HSM vendors and FIPS levels are supported for both hosted and private deployment? Is attestation evidence provided (e.g., certificate chains, firmware versions)?
3) Key provenance: how do you record the origin of a master key (customer-generated vs Redwood-generated) and can we export an immutable audit trail?
4) Rotation & rewrap: default rotation cadence, support for scheduled rotations, and how you re-encrypt stored ciphertext when a master key changes.
5) TLS profile: minimum TLS version, cipher suites, mutual TLS support for private endpoints, and certificate rotation process.
6) Live migrations: if we move from hosted to dedicated/private, how are keys migrated or re-provisioned safely?
7) Evidence: sample logs, import transcripts, and HSM attestation — will you provide a redacted bundle?

If you have a standard PDF or spreadsheet that maps answers to these items, please attach. Appreciate a short call if anything is unclear.

Best,
Evan

Head of Security

Evan / Stephanie — full technical response below. I'll flag items that are configuration-dependent for hosted vs private deployments.

1) BYO import paths and key handling- Supported import formats: PKCS#8 (PEM/DER), PKCS#12 (password-protected bundles), and wrapped-key import using AES-KWP (RFC 5649) or RSA-OAEP for asymmetric wrapping.
- Import flow (hosted): customer uploads an encrypted import blob via our control plane; import is performed within an HSM-backed import service that unwraps into a customer-specific master key slot. Customer secrets are never written to plaintext on disk; unwrapping occurs only inside FIPS-validated HSMs (see attestation).
- Import flow (private/VPC): customers may provide keys directly to their on-prem HSM or provide a wrapped blob for Redwood to import into the customer's HSM instance.
- Algorithms: RSA-2048/3072/4096 for RSA-OAEP wrapping, AES-128/256-KWP for symmetric wrapping. Supported key types: RSA, EC (P-256/P-384), and AES-256 (symmetric).

2) HSM vendors & attestation- Hosted: we operate FIPS 140-2 Level 2 and Level 3 HSMs depending on region and deployment tier (CloudHSM, Thales payShield-equipped clusters in dedicated regions).
- Private: supports Azure Dedicated HSM, AWS CloudHSM, and vendor-supplied Thales/HSM appliances.
- Attestation: we provide an attestation bundle including the HSM certificate chain, firmware versions, module serial numbers, and a time-stamped import transcript. For hosted customers we can provide redacted attestation; for private deployments we can assist retrieving on-site attestation statements.

3) Key provenance and immutable audit trail- Provenance metadata recorded at key creation/import: creator identity (user or service principal), import method, HSM slot id, timestamp, wrapping algorithm, and originating key fingerprint.
- Audit trail: all key lifecycle events (create/import, rotate, disable, destroy, export attempts) are captured in an append-only audit log shipped to the customer's audit sink (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) or to a syslog/SIEM via secure streaming. Logs include HSM attestation reference ids and a non-reversible event hash to help verify immutability.

4) Rotation & rewrap- Default policy: data keys (DEKs) rotated every 90 days; master keys (CMKs) rotation is customer-configurable.
- Rewrap strategy: when a CMK is rotated, DEKs that are envelope-wrapped are rewrapped lazily on first-decrypt (recommended for very large stores) or eagerly via a background rewrap job if requested. Both options maintain availability without downtime.
- Key versioning: we keep prior CMK versions for decryption of existing ciphertext; versions are time-bound and marked for archival or destruction per policy.

5) TLS profile and endpoint security- Public API (hosted): TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred. We disable known weak ciphers; reference matrix attached (tls_cipher_matrix.csv).
- Private/VPC: mutual TLS (mTLS) available for control-plane and data-plane endpoints; client cert rotation supported with automated cert revocation lists and ACME-like workflows for X.509 renewal.
- Certificate management: certs are rotated on a rolling schedule; in private deployments customers can integrate their internal PKI for automatic renewal.

6) Live migrations (hosted -> private/dedicated)- Key migration patterns:
  a) Re-provisioning: customer exports wrapped keys from Redwood into an RSA-OAEP-wrapped bundle and imports into their target HSM (preferred for customer-managed CMKs).
  b) Transit rewrap: for customers who require Redwood assistance, we perform an HSM-to-HSM key wrap inside an attested path (cross-HSM wrap) with dual-control approvals and an auditable transcript.
- We never export an unencrypted private key artifact outside an HSM without dual-operator authorization.

7) Evidence & artifacts- We will provide a redacted evidence bundle with: HSM attestation PDF, sample import transcript (scrubbed of any secrets), sample rotation logs, and sample audit-export manifest. Full un-redacted artifacts require NDA/addendum.

Attachments referenced: redwood_kms_byo_flow.pdf (process diagram), tls_cipher_matrix.csv (cipher mapping), evergreen_evidence_bundle.zip (redacted bundle).

If you want a short call to walk through any of the migration or rewrap options, suggest 30 minutes this week.

-Karthik

Senior Director, Infrastructure Security
